chapter: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band
title: E-flat versus double-B bass, Mac Walker, and slowing down Armstrong records
summary: Mac Walker could play the "West End Blues" introduction on E-flat tuba; Jones and Mac slowed Armstrong records at home to learn them, and his mother put him in the back yard to practice.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: What does that mean?
Well, that means what pitch the instrument is in.
Yeah.
See, some basses, it's double-B, you know.
Oh, I didn't know.
Double B-Flat. And some of them are E-Flat.
Oh. Why do they need the two pitches?

I don't know what that was. I know that the guys could get over the E-Flat better, because we had -- this guy I was telling you about, Mac, he could take that E-Flat tuba and he could play that introduction that Louis Armstrong played on, 'West End Blues.' (Singing). He could play that on that E-Flat. While the guys playing the double B-Flat, they couldn't make that.
Oh, yeah.
I don't know what it was.
The way it lay.
Yeah, the way it lay, and -- because we always used to wonder, you know, how they could get away with
that on that E-Flat bass. Before the bass fiddles had come into it, you know.
Yeah, right.
I think that's one reason why the Lloyd Scott took Mac, you know, because -- on the bass, because he was fast on it, you know, he could get over.
Yeah.

And he listened to those records, you know, Louis Armstrong's records, and we'd listen together when we'd go home, and we'd practice them. You had to forget it when you went back to Sunday school with the band, though.
Yeah.
We'd slow it down so we could hear what Louis was doing.
In your home?
Yes.
Did your mother say anything?
No. Didn't say a word. I guess she was happy we was in the house.
That you were doing it, yeah.

But sometimes she'd get a little peeved when I was there by myself, you know, and trying to practice things, you know, and they would give me a chair and set me out in the back yard. "Now sit back here and practice."
(Laughter)
